Choose the kind that matches the narrative intent; override the default with `multiplier` if the book specifies a non-standard value.

multiplier.description: Optional override for the damage multiplier. If omitted, the default for the `kind` is used (immunity=0, resistance=0.5, weakness=2.0). Use an explicit value for non-standard cases: 0.25 for 'heavy resistance', 1.5 for 'mild weakness', 3.0 for 'triple damage from fire on the fire-vulnerable troll'. Must be ≥ 0. Negative multipliers are not supported — an interaction cannot turn damage into healing; if a book needs that, use a modify_stat event or a round_script health adjustment instead. Values greater than 1 should use `kind: 'weakness'`; values less than 1 but greater than 0 should use `kind: 'resistance'`; 0 should use `kind: 'immunity'`. The emulator does not enforce this convention but the UI labels are chosen from `kind`, so mismatched values will display confusingly.

direction.description: Which damage flow the interaction applies to. `incoming` (default when absent) means damage dealt TO the enemy BY the player — the common case, used for 'enemy is immune to non-silver weapons' and similar rules. `outgoing` means damage dealt BY the enemy TO the player — used for 'player is resistant to fire damage while wearing the dragon amulet' or 'player takes double damage from this specific boss's breath weapon'. The emulator scales the relevant damage value (damage_to_enemy or damage_to_player) by the interaction's multiplier before subtracting from health.

source_has_any.description: Optional source-tag filter. If present and non-empty, the interaction applies only to damage components whose source list contains at least one of the listed tags. Examples: `['fire']` matches fire-tagged damage only; `['silver', 'blessed']` matches damage tagged silver OR blessed. Use this for 'double damage from fire' (weakness with source_has_any: ['fire']) or 'half damage from blunt or piercing' (resistance with source_has_any: ['blunt', 'piercing']). Omit (or use an empty array) for an interaction that should apply regardless of source tags. Source filtering is evaluated per-component per-round because a single attack can produce multiple damage components with different tags; this is what makes compound-damage cases like a poisoned silver weapon against a poison-immune silver-weak enemy work correctly. See Rule 18 for worked examples.

source_lacks_all.description: Optional inverse source-tag filter. If present and non-empty, the interaction applies only to damage components whose source list contains NONE of the listed tags. Canonical use: Helghast immunity — `{kind: 'immunity', source_lacks_all: ['silver', 'blessed', 'sommerswerd']}` → any damage component whose sources do not contain silver, blessed, or sommerswerd is zeroed. Damage tagged with `['silver']` bypasses the immunity because the component's sources include 'silver'; untagged damage (source list empty) is still matched because it contains none of the listed tags. The two source filters (`source_has_any` and `source_lacks_all`) can be combined on a single interaction — both must pass for the interaction to apply. See Rule 18 for worked examples.

condition.description: Optional gate evaluated once at combat start. Same condition union as combat_modifiers and event/choice conditions (`has_item`, `has_flag`, `stat_gte`, `stat_lte`, `has_ability`, `has_equipped_item`, `has_equipped_in_slot`, `has_equipped_with_property`, `not`, `and`, `or`, `test_failed`, `test_succeeded`). Condition filtering gates the entire interaction on player/world state; source filtering (`source_has_any` / `source_lacks_all`) gates per damage component on what the round_script emits. The two filters compose: a condition of `{has_equipped_with_property: 'holy'}` combined with `source_has_any: ['undead_slayer']` means 'this interaction applies only when the player has a holy-tagged equipped item AND the damage component is tagged with undead_slayer'. Condition filtering is frozen at combat start so mid-combat state changes do not re-evaluate. Null or absent means the interaction is not condition-gated.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of why the interaction applies. Shown in the combat UI's damage interactions panel so the player knows what's in effect, and written to the playthrough log when the interaction fires. Not interpreted by the emulator; purely for display and debugging. Examples: 'Helghast are harmed only by silvered or blessed weapons', 'Fire elemental is disrupted by cold', 'Skeleton is immune to poison', 'Undead take double damage from holy attacks'.

damage_cap.description: Schema v1.15+. A single per-encounter damage cap — an absolute upper bound on the post-interaction per-round damage total in a given direction. Caps live in two places: `damage_caps` on combat events (per-section situational rules) and `intrinsic_damage_caps` on enemies_catalog entries (rules that travel with the enemy type). Both use this same shape. The emulator evaluates each entry's optional `condition` once at combat start and freezes the passing entries; each round, after damage_interactions have scaled per-component damage and the components have summed into a per-direction total, every active cap matching that direction is applied as `total = min(total, cap.max)` (multiple matching caps compose by taking the smallest). Distinguished from `combat_modifier` (Rule 17 — additive deltas on round_script INPUTS) and `damage_interaction` (Rule 18 — multiplicative scaling on each damage COMPONENT) — caps are absolute bounds on the damage TOTAL after both prior layers run. Canonical example: Windhammer §564 Words of Protection (`any damage caused by Windhammer in each battle round will be limited to two endurance points` → `{max: 2, direction: 'outgoing', condition: {type: 'and', conditions: [{type: 'has_item', item: 'words_of_protection'}, {type: 'has_flag', flag: 'words_of_protection_uttered'}]}}`). See codex doc Rule 32 for the full specification.

max.description: Required. The absolute cap value applied to the post-interaction per-round damage total in the cap's direction. Must be ≥ 0. A cap of 0 zeroes the affected damage flow for the round (semantically similar to a `damage_interaction` of `kind: immunity` but applied to the total rather than per-component); a positive cap allows partial damage up to that maximum.

direction.description: Which damage flow the cap bounds. `outgoing` (default when absent) means damage dealt BY the enemy TO the player — the common case, used for protection-style rules like Windhammer §564 Words of Protection. `incoming` means damage dealt TO the enemy BY the player — used for rare cases where a fight has a cap on how much damage the player can deal per round (e.g., a sub-creature stage of a multi-form boss that takes at most N damage per round regardless of the player's roll). The emulator caps `damage_to_player` against `outgoing` caps and `damage_to_enemy` against `incoming` caps.

condition.description: Optional gate evaluated once at combat start. Same condition union as combat_modifiers and damage_interactions (`has_item`, `has_flag`, `stat_gte`, `stat_lte`, `has_ability`, `has_equipped_item`, `has_equipped_in_slot`, `has_equipped_with_property`, `not`, `and`, `or`, `test_failed`, `test_succeeded`). Condition filtering gates the entire cap on player/world state. Frozen at combat start; mid-combat state changes do not re-evaluate. Null or absent means the cap is not condition-gated and always applies for the fight's duration. Compound `and` / `or` / `not` conditions are first-class (canonical: §564 Words of Protection requires both the book in inventory AND the recorded-Word flag set).

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of why the cap applies. Shown in the combat UI's damage caps panel so the player knows what's in effect, and written to the playthrough log when the cap fires. Not interpreted by the emulator; purely for display and debugging. Examples: 'Words of Protection limits Windhammer's damage to 2 per round', 'Lich's curse: max 3 damage per round'.

min_attacker_margin.description: Schema v1.19+. Optional per-round gate that converts the cap into a gate-and-cap hybrid keyed on the round's attacker margin. When present, the cap's effective max for the round is computed as: if combat.attacker_margin >= min_attacker_margin, the cap applies normally with `max`; if combat.attacker_margin < min_attacker_margin, the cap blocks all damage in the cap's direction for that round (effective max of 0). Folds the gate-and-cap halves of source-text rules like 'the Dragon will only be able to harm you if it wins a combat round by more than N points... you can only lose a maximum of M points per round lost' into a single damage_cap entry (set min_attacker_margin to N+1, max to M). Round-script contract: the round_script must set combat.attacker_margin = <enemy_score - player_score> (or analogous source-text-defined margin) for the gate to evaluate. If combat.attacker_margin is unset or non-numeric when a min_attacker_margin cap is evaluated, the emulator logs a warning and skips the cap for that round. Canonical example: Windhammer §242 Shieldstone — `{max: 2, min_attacker_margin: 5, condition: <shieldstone_active>, direction: 'outgoing'}` encodes 'Dragon harms only on margin >= 5, capped at 2 EP per round.' Distinguished from `condition` (frozen at combat start, gates the entire fight) — min_attacker_margin is evaluated per round against the current round's attacker margin.

dice_amount.description: Schema v1.20+ (Rule 36). Dice-driven integer value rolled at firing time. Used as an alternative shape for `modify_stat.amount` in triggered_effects whose source text specifies a dice-driven heal or damage (canonical: GrailQuest healing potion bottle's 2d6 heal per dose). The emulator rolls `expression`, applies `sign`, and uses the rolled total as the integer delta. Strictly additive: the standard integer form of `modify_stat.amount` continues to validate unchanged.

expression.description: Dice expression in the same syntax as `roll_dice.dice` (e.g. '1d6', '2d6', '1d10+2'). The emulator rolls this at firing time and the rolled total becomes the delta.

sign.description: Whether the rolled total is added to or subtracted from the stat. Defaults to 'positive' when absent. For a 'lose 1d6 ENDURANCE' triggered effect, use `sign: negative`.

triggered_effect.description: Schema v1.20+ (Rule 36). A single run-time triggered effect that fires on a lifecycle event while the player is carrying / has-equipped an item, or has an ability / talent, or is fighting an enemy. Triggered effects live in four places: `items_catalog[].triggered_effects[]`, `enemies_catalog[].triggered_effects[]`, `rules.abilities.available[].triggered_effects[]`, and `rules.talents.available[].triggered_effects[]`. The emulator evaluates each entry's optional `condition` and optional `gate_roll` at the matching lifecycle point during play; passing entries dispatch their `effect`. Distinguished from: Rule 19 `stat_modifier.when` (passive while-carried/while-equipped stat deltas, frozen at combat start), Rule 25 `consume` (named-consumable eat_meal substitution, fires only at eat_meal pause), Rule 34 `effects[]` on abilities/talents (chargen-time auto-apply, fires once at choose_abilities/choose_talents confirm). The triggered_effects family handles run-time mechanics that fire repeatedly at well-defined lifecycle moments. See codex doc Rule 36 for the full specification, worked examples, and coexistence policy.

trigger.description: Lifecycle moment when the trigger fires. `while_equipped` fires once per combat round while the carrying item occupies its slot (implicit equipment check; only meaningful on `items_catalog[]`). `on_section_enter` fires once when the player enters any section. `on_section_exit` (schema v1.21+, Rule 36 v2.28.0 extension) fires once at the moment the player leaves a section — after every section event has resolved (including any combat win/lose/flee navigation) and BEFORE `state.currentSection` updates to the destination. Fires on every form of section-exit: choice navigation, combat-win, combat-lose, combat-flee. The trigger is the canonical home for per-section discipline / passive mechanics whose firing depends on what happened during the section (e.g. LW1's Healing Kai Discipline regen-if-no-combat); pair it with the `section_had_no_endurance_loss` and `section_had_no_combat` conditions for that mechanic's gate. `on_combat_start` fires once at combat start (after frozen modifiers / damage_interactions / damage_caps resolve). `on_combat_round` fires once per round during combat (after round_script and damage_interactions, before final-state apply). `on_combat_end` fires once at combat end regardless of outcome. `on_eat_meal` fires when an eat_meal pause is satisfied (orthogonal to Rule 25 `consume` — that one fires only when the player CHOOSES a named consumable). `on_rest` fires on a rest event (currently no rest event type ships; the trigger is reserved for source-text rest mechanics). `on_user_use` fires when the player explicitly clicks 'use' on the inventory entry (items only).

context.description: Meaningful only on `trigger: on_user_use`. Filters when the player may initiate use. `in_combat` = available only during a combat pause; `in_section` = available only between combats (not while a combat is active); `anywhere` (default when absent) = available at any time. Emulator UX freedom: the schema specifies the WHEN; the emulator decides the HOW (button placement, multi-use-per-pause, free-action vs round-cost). For other triggers this field is ignored.

condition.description: Optional gate evaluated at trigger-firing time. Same condition union as event conditions (`has_item`, `has_flag`, `stat_gte`, `stat_lte`, `has_ability`, `has_talent`, `is_equipped`, `has_equipped_item`, `has_equipped_in_slot`, `has_equipped_with_property`, `not`, `and`, `or`, `test_failed`, `test_succeeded`). Distinguished from `gate_roll` — the condition is a deterministic state check; the gate_roll is a dice-driven probabilistic gate. Both may be present on the same entry; both must pass for the effect to fire. Unlike damage_cap / combat_modifier conditions (frozen at combat start), triggered_effect conditions evaluate at each firing — mid-combat state changes do re-evaluate.

gate_roll.description: Optional probabilistic gate. The emulator rolls `dice` at firing time and the effect fires only if the rolled total matches `applies_on`. Use for source-text mechanics that say 'roll 1d6: on a 6, the shield reduces damage by 1'. Distinguished from `condition` — gate_roll is the per-firing dice gate; condition is the deterministic state check. Both may be present; both must pass.

dice.description: Dice expression in the same syntax as `roll_dice.dice` (e.g. '1d6', '2d6', '1d10').

applies_on.description: Inclusive numeric range or single face value as a string. Examples: '6' (single face), '1-2' (inclusive range), '1-5' (inclusive range), '10' (single face on 1d10). Same syntax as `roll_dice.results` keys. The effect fires when the rolled total falls within this expression.

effect.description: Required. The action that fires when trigger + optional condition + optional gate_roll all pass. See `triggered_effect_action` for the full discriminated union (damage-flow operations + flee_combat + reused non-pausing event types).

consume_on_fire.description: Meaningful only on `items_catalog[].triggered_effects[]`. When true, one copy of the carrying item is `remove_item`'d after the effect fires. Use for single-use scrolls and potions whose mechanic is fully captured by one trigger (e.g. `potion_of_invisibility` with `trigger: on_user_use` + `effect: flee_combat` + `consume_on_fire: true`). Default false. Multi-charge items (charges > 1) need a separate charges mechanism — deferred to a future schema bump.

reason.description: Optional human-readable explanation of what the triggered effect does and when. Shown by emulators in the inventory / ability detail panel and written to the playthrough log when the effect fires. Examples: 'Iron Shield with Golden Crescent: roll 1d6, on 6 reduce damage by 1', 'Potion of Invisibility: use to flee combat'.

oneOf.description: Schema v1.20+ (Rule 36). Damage-flow operation in the per-round damage pipeline. Pipeline ordering: Rule 17 combat_modifiers → Rule 18 damage_interactions → Rule 32 frozen damage_caps → Rule 36 shift/multiply/set (damage_delta, damage_multiplier, damage_set) → Rule 36 triggered caps (damage_cap) → apply to state. Multiple Rule 36 caps from different items compose by taking the smallest (extends the Rule 32 v1.15 tightest-cap-wins semantic across both cap layers). All four require `direction` (incoming = damage to enemy, outgoing = damage to player; the player's perspective is canonical).

direction.description: Which damage flow the operation affects. `outgoing` = damage out of the player's health (the player is hit). `incoming` = damage out of the enemy's health (the player hits). Player's perspective is canonical and matches the convention used by Rule 18 damage_interactions and Rule 32 damage_caps.

max.description: damage_cap: absolute upper bound on the per-round damage total in the direction. Composes with frozen Rule 32 caps and other Rule 36 caps by tightest-wins. A cap of 0 zeroes the affected damage flow for the round (semantically similar to immunity).

multiplier.description: damage_multiplier: multiplicative factor applied to the per-round damage total in the direction. Applied AFTER Rule 18 per-component damage_interactions and BEFORE Rule 36 triggered caps. Use 2 for 'double damage on this hit', 0.5 for 'half damage', 0 for 'no damage this round' (though damage_cap with max 0 is preferred for no-damage).

delta.description: damage_delta: signed integer shift applied to the per-round damage total in the direction. Use -1 for 'reduce damage by 1', +1 for 'extra damage this round'. Applied AFTER Rule 18 / Rule 32 frozen caps and BEFORE Rule 36 triggered caps. Final result is clamped to ≥ 0 (no negative damage).

oneOf.description: Symbolic expression evaluated at firing time. Currently 'enemy.max_health' is supported (writes the enemy's full health as the damage total, for vorpal-sword-style insta-kills). Future expressions may be added; books should not invent their own.

value.description: damage_set: absolute value to write as the per-round damage total in the direction, replacing whatever the upstream pipeline produced. Use for insta-kill mechanics (`{type: damage_set, direction: incoming, value: "enemy.max_health"}` on a vorpal sword 1d6-on-6) and similar source-text 'sets the damage to N' shapes. Rule 36 triggered caps applied AFTER this operation may still clamp it down.

oneOf.description: Schema v1.20+ (Rule 36). Flee-combat operation. Ends the active combat as a flee and navigates the player to `target_section`. Mirrors `combat.flee_to` but for source-text mechanics where the flee is driven by an item / ability / talent rather than a per-combat flee_to. Canonical example: Warlock potion_of_invisibility with `trigger: on_user_use` + `effect: {type: flee_combat, target_section: 105}`. If used outside of an active combat, the emulator logs a warning and skips the effect.

target_section.description: Section id to navigate to on flee. Integer or string (see codex 7.6.8 for string sub-section ids).

oneOf.description: Schema v1.26+ (Rule 42). Queue a one-shot combat modifier consumed on the next combat-enter. The single-use buff/debuff pattern: a consumable item (potion of strength, lucky charm), a cast spell, a narrative beat ('the wizard blesses you — your next fight has +2 COMBAT SKILL'), or any other source-text mechanic whose effect lasts 'for the duration of your next fight' and then clears. The emulator pushes the modifier onto `state.pendingCombatModifiers[]` at firing time; on the next `startCombat` invocation, the pending modifiers are drained into the combat's effective modifier set (frozen at combat start per Rule 17) and naturally fall away when combat ends. Canonical example: LW1's Alether (Potion of Strength) — `triggered_effects: [{trigger: on_user_use, consume_on_fire: true, effect: {type: queue_combat_modifier, modifier: {target: 'player.attack', delta: 2, reason: 'Alether Potion of Strength'}}}]`. If the player never enters another combat after queuing, the pending modifier stays buffered indefinitely (it is NOT a per-section timeout); this matches the source semantic ('swallow before a fight') where the player can choose when to cash in the buff. Multiple pending modifiers stack — drinking two potions before a combat yields both buffs.

modifier.description: The combat_modifier shape to queue. Same fields as Rule 17 combat_modifier entries: `target` (e.g., 'player.attack', 'enemy.attack', 'player.defense'), `delta` (signed integer), optional `reason` (display string). The queued modifier is merged into the next combat's effective modifier set at combat-start time, applying for the duration of that combat only.

target.description: What the modifier adjusts. Same vocabulary as Rule 17 combat_modifier.target — typical values 'player.attack', 'enemy.attack', 'player.defense', 'enemy.defense'.

delta.description: Signed integer to add to the target. +2 for a buff, -2 for a debuff.

reason.description: Optional display string surfaced when the modifier applies (e.g., 'Alether Potion of Strength', 'Wizard's blessing').

triggered_effect_action.description: Schema v1.20+ (Rule 36). Discriminated union over: (a) the existing non-pausing event types (`modify_stat`, `set_flag`, `clear_flag`, `add_item`, `remove_item`, `script`, etc. — same shape as the standard `event` definition); (b) the four new damage-flow operations (`damage_cap`, `damage_multiplier`, `damage_delta`, `damage_set`); (c) the new `flee_combat` operation. Interactive event types (`combat`, `stat_test`, `roll_dice`, `input_number`, `input_text`, `eat_meal`, `choose_items`, `return_to_caller`) MUST NOT appear here — triggered_effects are dispatched synchronously and cannot pause the section/combat flow.
